questions.question_text: In a particular box plot, the median line sits much closer to $Q_1$ than to $Q_3$, so the two halves of the box look very different sizes. Is this possible?

options.text: Yes — each half of the box holds $25\%$ of the data by count, not by an equal range of values
No — the median must be drawn exactly halfway between $Q_1$ and $Q_3$
options.why: Assumes the box is always split into two equal-width halves, which is only true when the data is evenly spread within it.

options.text: No — this would mean the box plot has been drawn incorrectly
options.why: Treats an unevenly split box as an error, when it correctly shows that the data is not evenly spread within the middle $50\%$.

options.text: Yes, but only if the dataset has a repeated value at the median
options.why: Adds an unnecessary condition — an off-centre median line reflects the spacing of the data values, not a repeated value.

questions.solution_text:
Each half of the box (from $Q_1$ to the median, and from the median to $Q_3$) holds exactly $25\%$ of the data by count.
The two halves cover the same number of data values, but not necessarily the same range of values — so the median line can sit off-centre.
